correctness.rationale: For 0<q<1,r>0 and odd L>=1, the meromorphic theta continuation of S_qr(t)=sum_n t^n/(1+r q^(2n)) has simple poles t=q^(2k) and multiplier S(q^2 t)=-r^-1 S(t). The odd power and Euler derivatives D^j S_(q,r^L) have matching negative multiplier. Their pole principal parts at t=1 form a triangular basis with diagonal j!, giving a degree L-1 polynomial with leading coefficient 1/(L-1)!. The pole-cancelled difference is holomorphic on C* and its global Laurent coefficients satisfy (q^(2n)+r^-L)b_n=0, forcing zero. Positive Cauchy products imply P(n)>0 on every integral index. For r=q cubic, P_3(n)=(n+1)(n+2)/2+3E(q); an exponentially dominated midpoint Riemann sum yields E(e^-h)~pi^2/(24h^2). Independently computed kernel/coefficients at multiple q,r,L with high precision.
